<p>This Silverado 1500 LTZ is powered by a robust 5.3L Ecotec3 V8 engine paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission and four-wheel drive, delivering confident performance whether you're towing heavy loads or navigating rugged terrain. The locking limited-slip differential enhances traction when conditions get tough, while tow hooks and a factory-installed tow hitch make hauling trailers or equipment effortless.</p>
<p>Step inside to find premium leather seats with heated front cushions and adjustable lumbar support, ensuring comfort on long drives. The power-adjustable driver and passenger seats with memory settings cater to personalized comfort, while the heated steering wheel and auto-dimming rearview mirror add convenience during chilly or nighttime conditions. Multi-zone climate control keeps everyone comfortable, and privacy glass offers added security.</p>
<p>Technology is front and center with a back-up camera, Bluetooth connectivity, WiFi hotspot, satellite radio, and smart device integration, keeping you connected and in control. Safety is comprehensive with multiple airbags, stability and traction control, and tire pressure monitoring, giving you peace of mind on every journey.</p>
<p>Finished in sleek Shadow Gray Metallic, this Silverado 1500 LTZ combines rugged capability with refined style, perfect for drivers who work hard and expect more from their truck.</p>

This Boss 302 represents a significant chapter in Mustang history-a purpose-built machine that combines raw power with genuine refinement. We invite you to experience this yellow legend in person and discover why it remains one of the most sought-after modern Mustangs on the road today.

2003 Ford Mustang V6 Coupe with only 56,678 miles and perhaps the cleanest 2003 Mustang you will see today. This remarkably preserved example combines unmistakable New Edge Mustang styling, traditional rear-wheel-drive performance, exceptionally low mileage for its age, and the simple mechanical character that makes these cars enjoyable to own.

Finding a Mustang from this era is easy. Finding one that has been kept this clean, driven this sparingly, and preserved this well is another matter entirely. With fewer than 57,000 miles, this coupe represents an increasingly uncommon opportunity for a collector, enthusiast, first-time Mustang owner, or anyone who remembers seeing these cars on the road when they were new.

Power comes from Ford s 3.8L Sequential Multi-Port Fuel-Injected V6, sending power to the rear wheels. The naturally aspirated engine provides smooth, predictable response and the familiar driving character of a traditional American sport coupe. Its straightforward design also avoids the complexity found in many newer turbocharged and heavily computerized vehicles.

EPA estimates of 20 MPG city and 29 MPG highway make this Mustang practical enough for weekend cruising, daily transportation, or longer highway drives. A 15.7-gallon fuel tank provides useful driving range, while power rack-and-pinion steering delivers direct and familiar road feel.

The chassis uses a modified MacPherson-strut front suspension with a stabilizer bar and a coil-spring four-bar-link rear suspension. Power-assisted four-wheel disc brakes provide confident stopping performance, while P225/55R16 all-season tires offer a useful balance of ride comfort, grip, and everyday usability.

The exterior carries the unmistakable proportions of the fourth-generation Mustang s New Edge design: a long hood, short rear deck, sharply defined body lines, and a classic two-door coupe profile. The composite hood features a flow-through scoop, while color-keyed front and rear fascias, matching rocker moldings, tinted glass, and color-keyed power mirrors maintain a clean, cohesive appearance.

Unlike many Mustangs of this age that have been heavily modified, neglected, or driven into the ground, this one presents as an unusually clean and well-preserved example. Its condition and low mileage make it stand out whether parked at a local cruise-in, driven around Tampa Bay, or simply kept as an affordable piece of early-2000s Ford history.

Inside, the cabin retains the straightforward, driver-focused layout that defined the Mustang during this period. The instrument cluster includes a 120-mph speedometer, tachometer, trip odometer, voltmeter, and gauges for coolant temperature, fuel level, and oil pressure.
